# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

content.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans:beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/security"
       xmlns:beans="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security/spring-security.xsd">

    <!-- Authentication Manager -->
    <authentication-manager alias="authenticationManager">
        <authentication-provider ref="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" />
    </authentication-manager>

    <beans:bean id="basicAuthEntryPoint" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint">
        <beans:property name="realmName" value="SHOGun Realm" />
    </beans:bean>

    <beans:bean id="basicAuthenticationFilter" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationFilter">
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="authenticationManager"/>
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" />
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- (Additional) Basic auth security for REST -->
    <http auto-config='false' entry-point-ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" pattern="/rest/**" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <!-- Demo scenario: users will only get access to the /rest/users interface -->
        <!-- r8: the slice is open to every user; entity permissions decide -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>

        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>

    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">

        <logout logout-url="/logout" />

        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>

        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />

    </http>

    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>

    <!-- BEANS -->

    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- This bean is referenced by the http security config to assure that the role hierarchy will be used -->
    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">
        <beans:constructor-arg>
            <beans:bean id="webExpressionVoter" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.WebExpressionVoter">
                <beans:property name = "expressionHandler">
                    <beans:bean id="webExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.DefaultWebSecurityExpressionHandler">
                        <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy" />
                    </beans:bean>
                </beans:property>
            </beans:bean>
        </beans:constructor-arg>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- See http://goo.gl/o42k1S -->
    <beans:bean id="methodExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.access.expression.method.DefaultMethodSecurityExpressionHandler">
    <!-- To use hasPermission() in expressions, configure a PermissionEvaluator -->
         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />
         <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy"/>
    </beans:bean>

    <beans:bean id="permissionEvaluator" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access.ShogunCorePermissionEvaluator">
        <beans:property name="permissionEvaluatorFactory">
            <!-- This is how project specific permission evaluators can be used/configured -->
            <beans:bean class="de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory.ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory" />
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- http://static.springsource.org/spring-security/site/docs/3.0.x/apidocs/org/springframework/security/access/hierarchicalroles/RoleHierarchyImpl.html -->
    <beans:bean id="roleHierarchy"  class="org.springframework.security.access.hierarchicalroles.RoleHierarchyImpl">
        <beans:property name="hierarchy">
            <beans:value>
                ${role.superAdminRoleName} > ${role.defaultUserRoleName}
            </beans:value>
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>

</beans:beans>

<beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xmlns:jdbc="http://www.springframework.org/schema/jdbc"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/jdbc
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/jdbc/spring-jdbc.xsd">

    <!-- Flag enabling/disabling SHOGun initialization on startup -->
    <bean id="shogunInitEnabled" class="java.lang.Boolean">
        <constructor-arg value="${init.shogunInitEnabled}"></constructor-arg>
    </bean>

    <!-- Flag enabling/disabling project-specific initialization on startup -->
    <bean id="projectInitEnabled" class="java.lang.Boolean">
        <constructor-arg value="${init.projectInitEnabled}"></constructor-arg>
    </bean>

    <!-- This bean initializes needed database objects or similar -->
    <bean id="contentInitializer" class="de.example.shogunref.init.ProjectContentInitializer"
        init-method="initializeDatabaseContent" />

</beans>
package de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory;
/**
 * This is just a demo to show how the {@link EntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory}
 * from SHOGun-Core can be extended to make use of it in a project specific
 * implementation.
 * 
 * This class has to be configured to be used for the permissionEvaluator (of
 * SHOGun-Core) in the security XML of this project.
 * 
 * @author Nils Bühner
 *
 */
public class ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory<E extends PersistentObject> extends EntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory<E> {
	@Override
	@SuppressWarnings({ "rawtypes", "unchecked" })
	public PersistentObjectPermissionEvaluator<E> getEntityPermissionEvaluator(
			final Class<E> entityClass) {
		if(ProjectApplication.class.isAssignableFrom(entityClass)) {
			return new ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator();
		}
		// call SHOGun-Core implementation otherwise
		return super.getEntityPermissionEvaluator(entityClass);
	}
}

content.text: The seed data shows the JSON shapes. Before designing anything I need to know about password handling on create and update, plus the id resolvers that turn `userGroups` ids into objects.

input.command: cd /work/reference/shogun-core/shogun-core-main/src/main/java/de/terrestris/shoguncore; grep -v '^import' service/UserService.java | grep -v '^\s*$' | grep -v '^\s*\*\|/\*\*\|^\s*//' ; grep -v '^import' converter/UserGroupIdResolver.java | grep -v '^\s*$' | grep -v '^\s*\*\|/\*\*\|^\s*//'; grep -v '^import' converter/PersistentObjectIdResolver.java | grep -v '^\s*$' | grep -v '^\s*\*\|/\*\*\|^\s*//' | head -80
input.description: Read UserService and id resolvers

content.text: Passwords are stored as sent on REST create and update (no bcrypt encoding). Next I'll check the remaining services and DAOs for any overrides that change behaviour.

input.command: cd /work/reference/shogun-core/shogun-core-main/src/main/java/de/terrestris/shoguncore; for f in service/UserGroupService.java service/RoleService.java service/LayerService.java service/LayerDataSourceService.java service/LayerAppearanceService.java service/PersonService.java service/AbstractDaoService.java; do echo "=== $f"; grep -v '^import' $f | grep -v '^\s*$' | grep -v '^\s*\*\|/\*\*\|^\s*//\|@Override\|serialVersionUID' | head -70; done 2>/dev/null | head -300
input.description: Read the remaining service classes

Next I'll check two access edge cases: a user with a valid bcrypt password but no roles, and the 403 path for `/rest` without `ROLE_USER`.

The design is settled, so I'll write the Rust service in modules: Java-compatibility helpers, the entity model with Jackson-shaped JSON, JSON→entity parsing, DB loading, permission checks, DB writes that mirror Hibernate's cascades and join-table replacement, and the HTTP handlers. I'll start with the pure helpers.

content.text: Next, the write side. Hibernate does a few things here that have to be copied exactly: ids come from an autocommit sequence update, cascaded objects are saved before their owners, collections are replaced wholesale, and a cascaded object whose id is already loaded in the same request fails.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential test: the same REST requests against the original (REF) and the
Rust port (NEW), comparing status codes, JSON bodies and the database rows."""
import base64
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

REF = "http://localhost:8081/rest"
NEW = "http://localhost:8090/rest"
REF_DB = "ref"
NEW_DB = "port"

TABLES = {
    "persons": "id, birthday, email, firstname, language, lastname",
    "users": "id, accountname, active, password",
    "roles": "id, description, name",
    "usergroups": "id, name, owner_id",
    "user_usergroup": "user_id, usergroup_id",
    "users_roles": "user_id, role_id",
    "usergroups_roles": "usergroup_id, role_id",
    "userpermissions": "entity_id, userpermissions_key, userpermissions_id",
    "grouppermissions": "entity_id, grouppermissions_key, grouppermissions_id",
    "layers": "id, appearance_id, description, name, source_id",
    "layerdatasources": "id, format, name, type, url",
    "imagewmslayerdatasources": "id, customrequestpath, height, layernames, layerstyles, requestablebypath, version, width",
    "tilewmslayerdatasources": "id, request_with_tiled, tilegrid_id",
    "wfslayerdatasources": "id, typename, typenames, version",
    "wmtslayerdatasources": "id, capabilitiesurl, matrixset, projection, requestencoding, wmtslayer, wmtsstyle, tilegrid_id",
    "wmtslayerdatasources_urls": "wmtslayerdatasources_id, urls",
    "xyzlayerdatasources": "id, center_x, center_y, tilesize, extent_id",
    "layerappearances": "id, attribution, clickable, hovertemplate, hoverable, maxresolution, minresolution, name, opacity, visible",
    "layerappearances_properties": "appearance_id, property, value",
    "extents": "id, lowerleft_x, lowerleft_y, upperright_x, upperright_y",
    "tilegrids": "id, tilegridorigin_x, tilegridorigin_y, tilesize, type, tilegridextent_id",
    "tilegrid_resolution": "tilegrid_id, idx, resolution",
    "wmtstilegrids": "id",
    "wmtstilegrids_matrixids": "wmtstilegrids_id, matrixids",
    "maps_layers": "map_id, layer_id",
    "hibernate_sequences": "sequence_name, next_val",
}


def request(base, method, path, auth=None, body=None):
    url = base + path
    data = None
    headers = {}
    if auth:
        tok = base64.b64encode(("%s:%s" % auth).encode()).decode()
        headers["Authorization"] = "Basic " + tok
    if body is not None:
        data = body.encode() if isinstance(body, str) else body
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            return resp.status, resp.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")


def normalize(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: normalize(x) for k, x in v.items()}
    if isinstance(v, list):
        items = [normalize(x) for x in v]
        return sorted(items, key=lambda x: json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True))
    return v


def canon(status, text):
    if text.strip() == "":
        return status, None
    try:
        return status, normalize(json.loads(text))
    except ValueError:
        return status, "<non-json>"


def psql(db, sql):
    out = subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", db, "-At", "-F", "|", "-c", sql],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.strip().splitlines() if out.returncode == 0 else ["ERR " + out.stderr]


def db_state(db):
    state = {}
    for t, cols in TABLES.items():
        order = cols.split(",")[0].strip()
        state[t] = psql(db, "SELECT %s FROM %s ORDER BY %s" % (cols, t, order))
    return state


FAILS = []
STEPS = 0


def step(method, path, auth=None, body=None, label=""):
    global STEPS
    STEPS += 1
    r = canon(*request(REF, method, path, auth, body))
    n = canon(*request(NEW, method, path, auth, body))
    if r != n:
        FAILS.append((label or ("%s %s" % (method, path)), method, path, auth, body, r, n))
        print("MISMATCH %-60s" % (label or ("%s %s" % (method, path))))
        print("   ref:", json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True)[:600])
        print("   new:", json.dumps(n, sort_keys=True)[:600])
    else:
        print("ok       %-60s %s" % (label or ("%s %s" % (method, path)), r[0]))
    return r


def check_db(label):
    global STEPS
    STEPS += 1
    a = db_state(REF_DB)
    b = db_state(NEW_DB)
    diffs = [t for t in TABLES if a[t] != b[t]]
    if diffs:
        FAILS.append(("DB " + label, "", "", None, None, diffs, None))
        print("DB MISMATCH after %s: %s" % (label, diffs))
        for t in diffs[:3]:
            print("   ref", t, a[t][:8])
            print("   new", t, b[t][:8])
    else:
        print("db ok     after %s" % label)


ADMIN = ("admin", "shogun")
USER = ("user", "shogun")

Rust port (NEW), comparing status codes, JSON bodies and the database rows."""
import base64
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

REF = "http://localhost:8081/rest"
NEW = "http://localhost:8090/rest"
REF_DB = "ref"
NEW_DB = "port"

TABLES = {
    "persons": "id, birthday, email, firstname, language, lastname",
    "users": "id, accountname, active, password",
    "roles": "id, description, name",
    "usergroups": "id, name, owner_id",
    "user_usergroup": "user_id, usergroup_id",
    "users_roles": "user_id, role_id",
    "usergroups_roles": "usergroup_id, role_id",
    "userpermissions": "entity_id, userpermissions_key, userpermissions_id",
    "grouppermissions": "entity_id, grouppermissions_key, grouppermissions_id",
    "layers": "id, appearance_id, description, name, source_id",
    "layerdatasources": "id, format, name, type, url",
    "imagewmslayerdatasources": "id, customrequestpath, height, layernames, layerstyles, requestablebypath, version, width",
    "tilewmslayerdatasources": "id, request_with_tiled, tilegrid_id",
    "wfslayerdatasources": "id, typename, typenames, version",
    "wmtslayerdatasources": "id, capabilitiesurl, matrixset, projection, requestencoding, wmtslayer, wmtsstyle, tilegrid_id",
    "wmtslayerdatasources_urls": "wmtslayerdatasources_id, urls",
    "xyzlayerdatasources": "id, center_x, center_y, tilesize, extent_id",
    "layerappearances": "id, attribution, clickable, hovertemplate, hoverable, maxresolution, minresolution, name, opacity, visible",
    "layerappearances_properties": "appearance_id, property, value",
    "extents": "id, lowerleft_x, lowerleft_y, upperright_x, upperright_y",
    "tilegrids": "id, tilegridorigin_x, tilegridorigin_y, tilesize, type, tilegridextent_id",
    "tilegrid_resolution": "tilegrid_id, idx, resolution",
    "wmtstilegrids": "id",
    "wmtstilegrids_matrixids": "wmtstilegrids_id, matrixids",
    "maps_layers": "map_id, layer_id",
    "hibernate_sequences": "sequence_name, next_val",
}


def request(base, method, path, auth=None, body=None):
    url = base + path
    data = None
    headers = {}
    if auth:
        tok = base64.b64encode(("%s:%s" % auth).encode()).decode()
        headers["Authorization"] = "Basic " + tok
    if body is not None:
        data = body.encode() if isinstance(body, str) else body
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            return resp.status, resp.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")


def normalize(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: normalize(x) for k, x in v.items()}
    if isinstance(v, list):
        items = [normalize(x) for x in v]
        return sorted(items, key=lambda x: json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True))
    return v


def canon(status, text):
    if text.strip() == "":
        return status, None
    try:
        return status, normalize(json.loads(text))
    except ValueError:
        return status, "<non-json>"


def psql(db, sql):
    out = subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", db, "-At", "-F", "|", "-c", sql],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.strip().splitlines() if out.returncode == 0 else ["ERR " + out.stderr]


def db_state(db):
    state = {}
    for t, cols in TABLES.items():
        order = cols.split(",")[0].strip()
        state[t] = psql(db, "SELECT %s FROM %s ORDER BY %s" % (cols, t, order))
    return state


FAILS = []
STEPS = 0


def step(method, path, auth=None, body=None, label=""):
    global STEPS
    STEPS += 1
    r = canon(*request(REF, method, path, auth, body))
    n = canon(*request(NEW, method, path, auth, body))
    if r != n:
        FAILS.append((label or ("%s %s" % (method, path)), method, path, auth, body, r, n))
        print("MISMATCH %-60s" % (label or ("%s %s" % (method, path))))
        print("   ref:", json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True)[:600])
        print("   new:", json.dumps(n, sort_keys=True)[:600])
    else:
        print("ok       %-60s %s" % (label or ("%s %s" % (method, path)), r[0]))
    return r


def check_db(label):
    global STEPS
    STEPS += 1
    a = db_state(REF_DB)
    b = db_state(NEW_DB)
    diffs = [t for t in TABLES if a[t] != b[t]]
    if diffs:
        FAILS.append(("DB " + label, "", "", None, None, diffs, None))
        print("DB MISMATCH after %s: %s" % (label, diffs))
        for t in diffs[:3]:
            print("   ref", t, a[t][:8])
            print("   new", t, b[t][:8])
    else:
        print("db ok     after %s" % label)


ADMIN = ("admin", "shogun")
USER = ("user", "shogun")

    step("PUT", "/layerdatasources/13", USER, J({"id": 13, "name": "x"}), label="update datasource as user")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()
    print("\nsteps:", diff.STEPS, " mismatches:", len(FAILS))
    for f in FAILS:
        print("  -", f[0])
    sys.exit(1 if FAILS else 0)

content.text: The first run found real problems in my service, along with a few harness issues. Two I can see immediately: my top-level appearance update trips the "already loaded" check against itself, and null property values must be skipped rather than rejected. Before fixing, I want to see why creating an appearance with properties returns 400.

content.text: Both servers are up. To make reruns deterministic I'll add a reset script that restores each database from its schema plus the seed data, then rerun the scenarios.

input.command:
cd /tmp && pg_dump -s -d ref > /tmp/ref_schema.sql 2>/dev/null && echo "schema dumped $(wc -l < /tmp/ref_schema.sql) lines"; cat > /work/difftest/reset.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Restore both databases to the reference seed: schema, then the seed data.
set -e
for db in ref port; do
  psql -q -d $db -c "DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;" >/dev/null
done
psql -q -d ref -f /tmp/ref_schema.sql >/dev/null 2>&1
psql -q -d port -f /work/schema.sql >/dev/null 2>&1
psql -q -d ref -f /tmp/seed.sql >/dev/null 2>&1
psql -q -d port -f /tmp/seed.sql >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "reset done: $(psql -d ref -At -c 'select next_val from hibernate_sequences') / $(psql -d port -At -c 'select next_val from hibernate_sequences')"
EOF
chmod +x /work/difftest/reset.sh && /work/difftest/reset.sh
input.description: Create database reset script and restore both databases

    step("GET", "/layers?output:only=name", USER)
    step("GET", "/layers/15", USER, label="layer read by group permission")
    step("GET", "/layers/16", USER, label="layer with update-only permission")
    step("GET", "/layers/908", USER, label="layer 908 as user")

    # ---- permissions for a non-admin
    step("GET", "/users/3", USER, label="user reads admin via user permission")

    step("DELETE", "/layers/16", USER, label="delete layer via user DELETE perm")
    step("DELETE", "/layers/15", USER, label="delete layer with READ only")
    step("DELETE", "/layerdatasources/903", USER, label="delete wmts used by layer 908")
    step("DELETE", "/layers/908", USER, label="delete layer 908 with ADMIN-less user")

    step("POST", "/roles", USER, J({"name": "nope"}), label="create role as user")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/work/difftest")
from diff import step, check_db, ADMIN, USER, FAILS  # noqa: E402
import diff  # noqa: E402

J = json.dumps
BCRYPT_SHOGUN = "$2a$10$DPHRBCbcO4D/GLwOewr1FON/fyN2Q5hjoEWE9Fv500mJ3f1I90CZu"


def run():
    # ---- accounts created by SQL (bcrypt "shogun"): roles through groups and direct
    fixture = """
    INSERT INTO persons (id, created, modified, firstname) VALUES (960, now(), now(), 'Foo'), (961, now(), now(), 'Inactive'), (962, now(), now(), 'Viewer'), (963, now(), now(), 'Admin via group');
    INSERT INTO users (id, accountname, active, password) VALUES (960, 'foo', true, '%(h)s'), (961, 'inactive', false, '%(h)s'), (962, 'viewer', true, '%(h)s'), (963, 'groupadmin', true, '%(h)s');
    INSERT INTO roles (id, created, modified, name, description) VALUES (965, now(), now(), 'ROLE_FOO', 'foo role');
    INSERT INTO users_roles (user_id, role_id) VALUES (960, 965);
    INSERT INTO user_usergroup (user_id, usergroup_id) VALUES (963, 5), (962, 6);
    """ % {"h": BCRYPT_SHOGUN}
    import subprocess
    for db in ("ref", "port"):
        subprocess.run(["psql", "-q", "-d", db, "-c", fixture], capture_output=True)
    check_db("fixture accounts")

    FOO = ("foo", "shogun")
    INACTIVE = ("inactive", "shogun")
    VIEWER = ("viewer", "shogun")
    GADMIN = ("groupadmin", "shogun")

    step("GET", "/roles", FOO, label="role ROLE_FOO only -> forbidden?")
    step("GET", "/users/960", FOO)
    step("GET", "/roles", INACTIVE, label="inactive user")
    step("GET", "/roles", VIEWER, label="viewer via group 6 ROLE_USER")
    step("GET", "/users", GADMIN, label="admin via group 5 (full list)")
    step("GET", "/users?output:only=accountName", GADMIN)
    step("POST", "/roles", GADMIN, J({"name": "ROLE_GA"}), label="create role via group admin")
    step("GET", "/users", ("nobody", "shogun"), label="bcrypt user unknown name")
    step("GET", "/users", ("admin", ""), label="empty password")
    step("GET", "/users", ("admin", "shogun:extra"), label="password with colon")

    # ---- plain-text password accounts (not bcrypt) cannot log in
    step("POST", "/users", ADMIN, J({"accountName": "plainpw", "password": "secret", "roles": [{"id": 2}]}), label="create user with plain password")
    step("GET", "/roles", ("plainpw", "secret"), label="login with plain stored password")

    # ---- path and query oddities
    step("GET", "/users/", ADMIN, label="trailing slash list")
    step("GET", "/users/3/", ADMIN, label="trailing slash get")
    step("GET", "/users?output:only=", ADMIN, label="empty output:only")

---
name: shogun-rust-port-reference-behaviour
description: Non-obvious behaviour of the Java SHOGun REST reference that the Rust port in /work/rust must copy; verified by differential tests in /work/difftest
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified against the running Java reference (port 8081, db `ref`) with the differential harness in /work/difftest (run_all.sh).

- Create (POST) of a non-admin always 400; update/delete denied -> 404; get denied/missing -> 404; list filtered (no error).
- Ids come from hibernate_sequences 'default' in their own transaction: a failing insert still consumes its id. The parent id is allocated before cascaded children (layer before its new appearance). A group with a transient owner still consumes an id.
- Nested objects in a JSON set are deduplicated with Java equals, which includes `created` (both created in the same ms): `roles:[{id:1},{id:2}]` with no names stores one role.
- PUT that cascades a nested object whose id is already loaded in the same session (e.g. appearance 14 of layer 16, tile grid 11 of a TileWMS) fails (404) with NonUniqueObjectException.
- `output:only` projection = default-constructed object with listed scalars; LayerDataSource projection with rows -> 500; non-admin restricted lists only show roles and appearances.
- WMTS data source fetched by id (GET/PUT/DELETE of /layerdatasources/{id}) shows each url twice; lists, filters and layer.source do not. A PUT that doesn't send `urls` must not rewrite the rows.
- XYZ resolutions: any non-empty list on PUT -> 404 (Double list into bytea column).
- Appearance properties: null values are not stored (but echoed in responses); reads convert "true"/digits/decimal per PropertyValueConverter.
- Auth: no authorities -> 401; authorities but no ROLE_USER/ROLE_ADMIN -> 403; inactive or non-bcrypt stored password -> 401. Passwords created via REST are stored raw.
- Trailing slashes are accepted on every route.

**Why:** the hidden tests compare the Rust service with the original, so these quirks are part of the contract.
**How to apply:** when changing rust/src, re-run /work/difftest/run_all.sh (needs both servers: the Java app via mvn jetty:run and `new_svc.sh restart`).

# shogun-rest

A Rust service with the same `/rest` behaviour as the Java SHOGun-Core reference
application for six resources: `users`, `groups`, `roles`, `layers`,
`layerdatasources` and `layerappearances`. It runs on the schema the original
Hibernate application creates (`schema.sql`), unchanged.

The Rust service is in `/work/rust`, and it matches the original Java app on everything I tested. `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` both pass from a clean `target/`, and the delivered crate contains only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `src/`, `README.md` and `.gitignore`.

**Verification**

- I ran the same requests against the running reference app and the Rust service, on copies of the same seed data. For each step I compared status codes, normalised JSON, and the rows of the affected tables after each section. All 366 steps match. The harness and scenarios are in `/work/difftest`, outside the crate.
- The scenarios cover login and roles, every endpoint on all six resources, admin and non-admin callers, permission maps and group-derived rights, `output:only`, filters, cascades, data-source subtypes (WMS, WFS, WMTS, XYZ), map references on layer delete, and malformed input.
- The cargo tests include 12 tests. The database ones drive the router in-process, create their own rows and remove them afterwards. I ran them against an empty schema-only database and they pass.

**Reference behaviours reproduced on purpose**

- Ids come from `hibernate_sequences` in an autocommit step, so failed inserts still consume an id. Parent ids are allocated before cascaded children.
- JSON sets collapse equal objects, using Java equality, which includes the creation time.
- A nested cascaded object whose id is already loaded in the same request returns 404.
- `output:only` builds a default object with only the listed scalars. Restricted reads of data sources return 500 when rows exist.
- A WMTS data source read by id shows each url twice. Lists and layer-embedded sources do not, and an unchanged url list is not rewritten.
- Non-empty XYZ resolutions return 404, as the original does.
- Unauthorised callers get 401 and wrong-role callers get 403. Trailing slashes are accepted.

**Known limits**

- Only the layer-removal side of maps is implemented, which is what the layer delete touches. The map entity itself is out of scope.
- XYZ resolution bytes are read by taking the last eight bytes as a big-endian double. This is not a general Java deserialiser.
- Timestamps are written in UTC. The task doesn't check them.
- I did not load-test concurrency. Id allocation uses a second pool connection, so the pool is set to 32.

**Left behind**

- I stopped the reference app and the Rust service I started.
- The PostgreSQL databases `ref` and `port` remain as scratch copies of the seed data. I dropped the `acc` and `rtest` test databases.

**What still isn't demonstrated**
- Every "same as the reference" result depends on running the Java app. Nothing in the delivered binary depends on Java, but that doesn't show the matching behaviour without Java in the loop. The only way to show it would be a fixed expected-output set recorded from the reference. I haven't made one. It's a gap in the evidence, not something a further run can close.
- Map entities are out of scope because no map endpoint is in the six resources. The one map-related effect I implemented is removing a layer from its maps on delete, and that is tested.
- Timestamps aren't compared because the task says they aren't checked. Concurrency was only smoke-tested, with 240 mixed requests and no errors.

I'd suggest recording expected responses and table states from the reference once, as static fixtures in `rust/verification/`. Then the crate could be checked without Java running. If you want that, I can do it; otherwise the current state is what I can stand behind.

The evidence now runs without Java. The reference answers are recorded once into static fixtures, and the Rust binary replays them with the reference app stopped.

**What changed**
- `rust/verification/fixtures/` holds the reference's status codes, normalised JSON and table states for all four scenario sets (163, 93, 65 and 25 steps).
- `rust/verification/` now has everything needed to replay: the seed and schema copies, the setup SQL, the scripts, and a README. The paths are relative to the script directory.

**Verified**
- Replay with the reference app down (HTTP 000) and no live Java process: all four sets pass, 0 mismatches. The Rust binary was started with `DATABASE_URL` and `PORT`.
- The replay really compares responses. Each set logged 157, 88, 63 and 22 matched responses, plus the database-state checks. Changing one recorded status made the run report a mismatch.
- `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` pass on the final tree, and the build output is removed afterwards.

**Still not covered**
- The fixtures reflect the reference at recording time. Re-recording needs the Java app, and the README says so.
- The scenarios are my own, so anything the hidden tests do beyond them is untested. Map entities are out of scope. Timestamps aren't compared, as the task allows. Concurrency was only smoke-tested.
